name: first-principles
title: Differentiation from first principles
tagline: Curve with a point, tangent and shrinking chords for first principles; gradients derived; draw-tangent answer mode (pivot a line until tangent) and science axis titles.
description: A curve y = f(x) with a point P = (a, f(a)) on it, its tangent, and chords (secants) from P to Q = (a+h, f(a+h)) — the model for differentiation from first principles and for tangents/gradients. You give the function as an expression ("x^2", "x^3 - 2x"), the point a, and the chord increments h; the model derives everything quantitative — the tangent and its gradient f′(a) (numeric derivative), each chord and its gradient [f(a+h) − f(a)] / h, the point Q, and the δx/δy rise-run triangle. The headline interaction is the h-slider: drag h towards 0 and the live chord rotates onto the tangent (the limit, before your eyes). For print, draw several static chords with shrinking h to show the same convergence. Optionally overlay the whole gradient function y = f′(x). Occlude a gradient for a "find f′(a)" question; highlight the answer. Web: the h-slider, dragging P along the curve, or dragging a chord's Q. Answer on the model (@2): set drawTangent: true and host with responseMode "draw-tangent" to pose "draw the tangent at x = a" — the posed surface shows the curve and the marked point with NO tangent (a blank answer space); armed, a deliberately wrong pre-placed line through the point pivots as the pupil drags, and the model self-checks their gradient against the derived f′(a) within gradientTolerance (default: a ±5° by-eye band); correctAnswer is the { derived: true } sentinel and the true tangent never reaches any surface. Axis titles (@2): axes.labels { x, y } prints quantity + unit titles ("time (s)", "volume of gas (cm³)") so rates-of-reaction and other science curves carry honest labelled axes.
whenToUse: Reach for this to teach differentiation from first principles, the tangent to a curve and its gradient, the chord/secant and the limit as h → 0, or to plot the gradient function f′(x). Give fn as an expression of x (same syntax as function-graph: + - * / ^, parentheses, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt cbrt abs exp ln log, pi and e, implicit multiplication like "2x" and "3sin(x)"; trig in radians), set point.x = a, and choose chords by their increment h. The classic interactive build is one point plus hSlider: { min: 0, max: 3 } — pupils drag h towards 0 and watch the chord rotate onto the tangent (at h = 0 it lands on it); or, equivalently, one point + a single chord + draggable so they drag the chord's far end towards P. For a static (print/slide) version use the chords array, h = 2, 1, 0.5 fanning down onto the tangent, each gradient shown approaching f′(a). Use point alone (tangent: true) for "the tangent at x = a and its gradient"; add gradientCurve to motivate the derivative as a function. Set occludeGradient to ask "work out the gradient", highlight to mark the answer, point.guides for dashed lines to the axes, chord.triangle for the rise-run right triangle with δx and δy legs. Keep the same window across a lesson's blocks so chords compare on a fixed frame, and choose the y-range so both P and the far chord end Q are in view. Draw the tangent ON the model (auto-marked, @2): for every "draw the tangent to the curve at x = a" question — including the GCSE science staple "draw the tangent at t = 30 s and use it to find the rate" — host a marked model tile with responseMode "draw-tangent", params drawTangent: true and point: { x: a } (tangent is forced off on every surface; the pupil pivots a pre-placed wrong line about the point until it lies tangent). Set gradientTolerance to the mark scheme's accepted gradient half-band when the scheme states a range (accepted range 0.2–0.4 → the point where the centre is derived and gradientTolerance: 0.1); omit it for the default by-eye allowance (±5° of screen angle about the true tangent). There is no live gradient readout while dragging — reading the gradient off the drawn tangent's triangle is the follow-up question's skill, so pair this tile with a typed/math question for the gradient value ("use your tangent to estimate the rate at t = 30 s"). Science graphs (@2): give the axes quantity + unit titles with axes.labels: { x: "time (s)", y: "volume of gas (cm³)" }, identical across a lesson's blocks; keep the same window as the paired function-graph plot so the two figures compare. Switch primitive when the teaching changes — to sketch or read a curve's roots/turning points/asymptotes use graphing/function-graph; for the area under a curve, the trapezium rule or Riemann strips use graphing/area-under-curve; for a distance-time or speed-time gradient use graphing/journey-graph; for a graphical inequality region use graphing/inequality-region. Synonyms a teacher might use: differentiation, derivative, first principles, from first principles, gradient, gradient of a curve, tangent, draw a tangent, chord, secant, rate of change, instantaneous rate, rate of reaction, dy/dx, f prime, gradient function, limit, h tends to zero, delta x.

axes.description: The window — the rectangle of the plane shown. Frame it so the point P and the far end of every chord are visible with a little room.

y.description: [min, max] for the y-axis. Default [-10, 10]. Include the heights of P and the chord ends.

xStep.description: Gap between x gridlines / axis numbers. Default: a sensible round value.

yStep.description: Gap between y gridlines / axis numbers. Default: a sensible round value.

equalAspect.description: Force TRUE square scale (1 x-unit = 1 y-unit in pixels) so a stated gradient looks like the right slope on screen. Default false (x and y scaled independently to fill the box). Set true when the visual steepness of the tangent must read accurately.

degrees.description: Evaluate trig in degrees rather than radians. Default false. Rarely needed here.

labels.description: Axis titles — the quantity and unit each axis measures, e.g. { x: "time (s)", y: "volume of gas (cm³)" }. A bare variable letter (up to 3 characters, e.g. "t") prints in the house axis-name style (x just past the x-arrow tip, y above the y-arrow tip); a quantity + unit title prints in the exam-paper position (x centred below the plot, y at the top-left canvas edge) so the figure keeps its size. Use on science/experimental curves (rates of reaction, cooling curves), identical across a lesson's blocks. Omit for a plain maths figure (default: no titles).

x.description: Title for the horizontal axis, quantity then unit in brackets: "time (s)". A bare variable letter ("t") also works.

y.description: Title for the vertical axis: "volume of gas (cm³)", "mass (g)".

grid.description: Show the background grid. Default true.

fn.description: The function f(x) as an expression: + - * / ^, parentheses, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt cbrt abs exp ln log, pi and e, implicit multiplication. Trig in radians. Examples: "x^2", "x^3 - 2x", "1/x", "sin(x)".

label.description: Equation label drawn near the curve, e.g. "y = x²". Use proper typography (², −). Omit for an unlabelled curve.

point.description: P — the point on the curve where you differentiate / draw the tangent. Its coordinates (a, f(a)) and the tangent's gradient f′(a) are DERIVED; you give only a.

x.description: The x-value a. P sits at (a, f(a)) on the curve.

label.description: Name shown at P (e.g. "P"). Omit to show the derived coordinates.

tangent.description: Draw the tangent line at P (its gradient f′(a) is derived numerically). Default true.

showGradient.description: Print the derived tangent gradient f′(a) beside the tangent. Default true.

occludeGradient.description: Hide the tangent gradient as "?" — the "work out f′(a)" hook. The tangent still shows. Default false.

guides.description: Dashed guide lines from P to each axis. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to P and its tangent (amber). Default false.

chords.description: Secant lines from P to Q = (a + h, f(a + h)) — the first-principles chords. Each chord's gradient [f(a+h) − f(a)] / h is derived. List several with shrinking h (e.g. 2, 1, 0.5) to show the chord gradient approaching the tangent gradient. Requires point.

h.description: The increment. Q = (a + h, f(a + h)). Positive = chord to the right of P, negative = to the left. Avoid exactly 0.

triangle.description: Draw the rise-run right triangle under the chord with its legs labelled δx ( = h) and δy ( = f(a+h) − f(a)). Default false.

label.description: Override the chord's gradient readout text. Omit to show the derived gradient.

occludeGradient.description: Hide this chord's gradient as "?". Default false.

highlight.description: Amber emphasis on this chord. Default false.

gradientCurve.description: Overlay the derived gradient function y = f′(x) (the numeric derivative of fn sampled across the window) as a second curve — motivates the derivative as a function. Default false.

hSlider.description: The first-principles slider — the headline interaction. A single live chord is drawn at h = value with a slider above the graph; dragging it toward the minimum shrinks h so the chord rotates ONTO the tangent (the limit, interactively), and the chord gradient closes on f′(a). Keep the tangent on (default) so the chord visibly approaches it, and use min 0 so the slider reaches the limit — at h = 0 the chord coincides with the tangent. The static chords array is the print fallback for the same idea. Web-only.

min.description: Smallest h the slider reaches. Use 0 so the chord can shrink the whole way to the limit — at h = 0 the chord lands exactly on the tangent.

max.description: Largest h — the chord at its most open, e.g. 3.

value.description: Starting h. Default: max (start open, then drag in towards 0).

step.description: Snap h to multiples of this. Omit for a continuous slider.

drawTangent.description: The "draw the tangent at x = a" ANSWER surface (@2, responseMode "draw-tangent"). Requires point (the touch point x = a — the question names it) and fn. On EVERY surface the tangent, its gradient, the gradient curve, chords, the h-slider and exploratory dragging are forced off — posed (print/PPTX, no response ctx) the figure is the curve + marked point, a blank answer space the pupil draws on with a ruler. Armed on a web question, a deliberately WRONG pre-placed line through the point pivots as the pupil drags anywhere along it; the model self-checks the pupil's gradient against the derived f′(a) inside its enhance closure (the true tangent is never drawn and never in the markup). correctAnswer is the { derived: true } sentinel. Default false.

gradientTolerance.description: draw-tangent only: half-band (in gradient units) the pupil's tangent gradient may differ from the derived f′(a) and still be correct — set it to mirror a mark scheme's stated range (accepted rate 0.2–0.4 → gradientTolerance 0.1). Default: the by-eye allowance, ±5° of on-screen angle about the true tangent.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. the function being differentiated. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

draggable.description: Web-only. With a chord present, P is the FIXED target and you drag the chord's far end Q along the curve — towards P shrinks h so the chord rotates onto the tangent (drag it all the way onto P to reach the limit); the chord gradient closes on f′(a) live. With NO chord, P itself is dragged along the curve so the tangent and its gradient change. Default false.
